subject.title: Feishu: duplicate final replies can occur after model failover from rate-limited primary

question: Where should the permanent duplicate-final guard for Feishu model-failover recovery live: Feishu dispatcher, shared final dispatch, or the broader durable final-delivery contract?
rationale: The source evidence shows a real bug, but the fix boundary affects which distinct finals remain visible across channel and failover paths, which is a product and owner-boundary choice rather than a safe autonomous repair.

options.title: Approve focused Feishu plus final-dispatch repair
options.body: Define the failover-specific invariant, preserve intentional distinct finals, and require Feishu/source regression proof before landing.

options.title: Fold into durable final-delivery contract
options.body: Treat this as one acceptance case for the broader channel delivery semantics work and avoid a standalone Feishu fix until that contract is chosen.

options.title: Use only a narrow Feishu workaround
options.body: Patch Feishu streaming closeout locally, accepting that non-streaming or shared failover duplicate paths may remain separately tracked.

recommendation.title: Approve focused Feishu plus final-dispatch repair
recommendation.body: Define the failover-specific invariant, preserve intentional distinct finals, and require Feishu/source regression proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans shared reply-dispatch contracts and Feishu channel boundaries where this history shows prior refactor and hook ownership.
